name: Consumer genomics and health testing
title: Consumer genomics after 23andMe and Arivale: the board abstains
question: Is consumer genomics viable again after 23andMe and Arivale?
answer: Reading a whole genome cost about $95M in 2001 and a few hundred dollars by 2022 (NHGRI). Yet Arivale, a genome-based wellness subscription, closed in 2019, and 23andMe filed for bankruptcy in March 2025. When the named constraint has fallen by a factor of 100,000 and the category still dies, cost was not the binding constraint, and the board does not know what is.
verdict_reason: The named constraint crossed long ago and the category died anyway, so the rule abstains.

constraint.name: Cost of sequencing (named, but not binding)
constraint.detail: Cost was the obvious blocker and it collapsed. Repeat purchase and clinical usefulness are the likelier blockers, and neither has a public metric.

metric.label: Cost to sequence a human genome (NHGRI, via Our World in Data)
metric.source_note: NHGRI measured cost, not vendor list prices

graveyard.name: Arivale
graveyard.how: Closed abruptly in April 2019, saying its service cost more than customers would pay
